Thanks for the ping, Jonas. Quick guidance and next steps from Legal: 

- Controller/Processor: From the template language, RedOak considers Redwood a processor. We'll use our standard DPA wording but will review SCC applicability if RedOak's data flows cross EEA borders. If so, we'll propose the EU SCCs + appropriate annex.
- International transfers: ask RedOak to confirm data residency (US-only vs EEA). If US-only, SCCs may not be needed; if EEA->US flows exist, we'll provide recommended SCC language.
- DPIA responses: we'll provide redline suggestions for any admissions that might be construed as shifting liability.

I will draft the legal language by end of day 2026-03-14. Marissa, can you drop a two-paragraph control description and attach the retention table?

Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Hi all — attaching the operational artifacts and a short control summary. Summary below:

- Data flows & isolation: for Hosted, requests are multi-tenant but logically separated; for Dedicated/Private we run tenant-resident compute and provide VPC controls.
- Retention: default conversational content retention is 90 days (configurable by contract); logs retained 12 months. We can propose a contract amendment for shorter retention if required.
- Incident response: 1 hour detection triage SLA (internal), 6 hours customer notification SLA for high-severity incidents; playbook excerpt attached.

Attachments: DPIA_RedOak_Response_v1.xlsx (filled answers draft), RDW_SOC2_Type2_Redwood_2025.pdf (link repeated)

Happy to jump on a 30m call with the RedOak team to walk through the answers — propose Monday 3/15 10:00am PT.

Marissa Cole
